course.title: Wig Making
course.tagline: Make and style wigs from scratch: measuring, ventilating, styling and selling your first unit.

days.title: Welcome to Wig Making
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Your kit is a wig cap, canvas head, needles, thread, bundles, lace and a mannequin head.

video.title: How to Make a Lace Frontal Crochet Wig Using One Pack of Braiding Hair

steps: Get your tools ready: canvas block head, curved needle and wig cap.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A canvas block head holds the wig cap steady while you sew.
Your kit is a wig cap, canvas head, needles, thread, bundles, lace and a practice head. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise welcome to wig making on a model or a practice head. Your kit is a wig cap, canvas head, needles, thread, bundles, lace and a practice head. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do welcome to wig making two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: Why do you use a canvas block head when you sew a wig?
options: It cuts the bundles to the right length.
It holds the wig cap steady while you sew.
It dries the wig faster after washing.
It colours the hair for you.
quiz.explain: A canvas block head holds the wig cap steady while you sew.

quiz.q: What is in your wig-making kit?
options: A wig cap and a canvas head only.
A flat iron, a curling wand and hair spray.
A wig cap, canvas head, needles, thread, bundles, lace and a practice head.
Scissors, dye and a shower cap.
quiz.explain: Your kit is a wig cap, canvas head, needles, thread, bundles, lace and a practice head.

quiz.q: What should you do with your needles when you are not using them?
options: Stick them in the wig hair.
quiz.explain: Keep needles capped when not in use, so nobody gets pricked.

days.title: Measuring the Head
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Measure the circumference, front to nape and ear to ear so the cap fits perfectly.

video.title: How to Bleach the Knots on a Lace Frontal

steps: Get your tools ready: canvas block head, curved needle and wig cap.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Head measurements decide the size of the wig cap.
Measure the circumference, front to the back of the neck and ear to ear so the cap fits perfectly. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise measuring the head on a model or a practice head. Measure the circumference, front to the back of the neck and ear to ear so the cap fits perfectly. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do measuring the head two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: Why do head measurements matter when you make a wig?
options: Head measurements decide the size of the wig cap.
Measurements tell you what colour to use.
Measurements tell you how long the wig should be.
Measurements decide the price of the wig.
quiz.explain: Head measurements decide the size of the wig cap.

quiz.q: Which three measurements do you take so the cap fits well?
options: Circumference, front to nape, and ear to ear.
Hair length, hair colour, and head shape.
Neck size, shoulder width, and arm length.
quiz.explain: Measure the circumference, front to nape and ear to ear so the cap fits perfectly.

quiz.q: What happens if you skip measuring the head?
options: The cap may be too big or too small.
quiz.explain: Head measurements decide the size of the wig cap, so skipping them risks a bad fit.

days.title: Choosing Hair and Lace
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Pick human or synthetic hair and a lace type: closure, frontal or full lace.

video.title: How to Pluck the Lace on a Frontal

steps: Get your tools ready: canvas block head, curved needle and wig cap.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A wide lace frontal gives a wider, more natural-looking parting than a small lace closure.
Pick human or synthetic hair and a lace type: a closure (small lace piece), a frontal (wide lace piece) or full lace. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise choosing hair and lace on a model or a practice head. Pick human or synthetic hair and a lace type: a closure (small lace piece), a frontal (wide lace piece) or full lace. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do choosing hair and lace two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: Why choose a wide lace frontal instead of a small closure?
options: It makes the wig dry faster.
It gives a wider, more natural-looking parting.
quiz.explain: A wide lace frontal gives a wider, more natural-looking parting than a small lace closure.

quiz.q: What are the three lace types you can pick?
quiz.explain: Pick a closure (small lace piece), a frontal (wide lace piece) or full lace.

quiz.q: What two things do you choose when you plan a wig?
options: The hair type and the lace type.
The colour and the length only.
quiz.explain: Pick human or synthetic hair and a lace type: closure, frontal or full lace.

days.title: Cap Construction Basics
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Stretch the cap on the block, pin it, and mark the hairline before sewing.

video.title: Step By Step| How to Make a Wig Like a Pro for Beginners Hand Sewn & Sewing Machine Method |WestKiss

steps: Get your tools ready: canvas block head, curved needle and wig cap.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: The cap must be pinned flat on the block before sewing.
Stretch the cap on the block, pin it, and mark the hairline before sewing. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise cap construction basics on a model or a practice head. Stretch the cap on the block, pin it, and mark the hairline before sewing. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do cap construction basics two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What must you do to the cap before you start sewing?
options: Pin it flat on the block.
quiz.explain: The cap must be pinned flat on the block before sewing.

quiz.q: What do you mark on the cap before sewing?
quiz.explain: Stretch the cap on the block, pin it, and mark the hairline before sewing.

quiz.q: Why cap your needles when you stop sewing?
quiz.explain: Keep needles capped when not in use, so nobody gets pricked.

days.title: Sewing Wefts
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Sew wefts in a U-shape from the nape upward, folding the weft at each turn.

video.title: Wig Making 101 Series| Laying Tracks/Weft (Best Way for Fit)

steps: Get your tools ready: canvas block head, curved needle and wig cap.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Strips of hair (called wefts) are sewn from the back of the neck upward in rows.
Sew strips of hair (called wefts) in a U-shape from the back of the neck upward, folding the weft at each turn. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise sewing wefts on a model or a practice head. Sew strips of hair (called wefts) in a U-shape from the back of the neck upward, folding the weft at each turn. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do sewing wefts two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: Which way do you sew wefts onto the cap?
options: From the back of the neck upward in rows.
From side to side in one long row.
quiz.explain: Strips of hair (called wefts) are sewn from the back of the neck upward in rows.

quiz.q: What shape do you sew the wefts in?
options: A straight line with no folds.
A U-shape, folding the weft at each turn.
A circle around the whole cap.
quiz.explain: Sew wefts in a U-shape from the nape upward, folding the weft at each turn.

quiz.q: What should you do with the needle each time you stop to check your work?
quiz.explain: Keep needles capped when not in use, so nobody gets pricked.

days.title: Making a Closure Wig
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Sew a 4x4 closure at the front, then wefts behind it to the nape.

video.title: Creating Natural Edges on a Lace Wig

steps: Get your tools ready: canvas block head, curved needle and wig cap.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A 4x4 closure gives a four-inch square parting space.
Sew a small square lace closure at the front, then strips of hair (wefts) behind it to the back of the neck. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise making a closure wig on a model or a practice head. Sew a small square lace closure at the front, then strips of hair (wefts) behind it to the back of the neck. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do making a closure wig two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: How big is the parting space on a 4x4 closure?
quiz.explain: A 4x4 closure gives a four-inch square parting space.

quiz.q: Where do you sew the closure on a closure wig?
options: At the front, with wefts behind it to the nape.
At the back, with wefts in front of it.
On the side, with wefts on the other side.
Under the cap, where nobody can see it.
quiz.explain: Sew a 4x4 closure at the front, then wefts behind it to the nape.

quiz.q: How do you store your needle between sewing steps?
options: Leave it loose in the bundles.
quiz.explain: Keep needles capped when not in use, so nobody gets pricked.

days.title: Making a Frontal Wig
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Place a 13x4 frontal at the hairline, sew it flat, then add wefts behind.

video.title: How to Make a Lace Front Wig

steps: Get your tools ready: canvas block head, curved needle and wig cap.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: A 13x4 frontal spans ear to ear across the hairline.
Place a wide lace frontal at the hairline, sew it flat, then add strips of hair (wefts) behind. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise making a frontal wig on a model or a practice head. Place a wide lace frontal at the hairline, sew it flat, then add strips of hair (wefts) behind. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do making a frontal wig two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: How far does a 13x4 frontal reach?
options: From the crown to the nape only.
Across the back of the head only.
Ear to ear across the hairline.
From one side of the neck to the other.
quiz.explain: A 13x4 frontal spans ear to ear across the hairline.

quiz.q: Where do you place the frontal on a frontal wig?
options: On top of the crown only.
At the hairline, sewn flat, with wefts behind.
quiz.explain: Place a 13x4 frontal at the hairline, sew it flat, then add wefts behind.

quiz.q: What is the safe habit when you put your needle down?
options: Balance it on the block head.
quiz.explain: Keep needles capped when not in use, so nobody gets pricked.
